metadata.title: Ant Lingbo's Shen Yujun on Robot-Native Foundation Models: Brain, Body, and Data
metadata.guest_role: Chief Scientist, Ant Lingbo (Tang Xiao'ou lineage)

conclusion: After last episode's Physical Intelligence (π) deep dive, Zhang turns to a domestic brain-first sample: Shen Yujun, chief scientist at Ant-incubated Ant Lingbo. The industry twist — Chinese teams starting from robot brains then filling in bodies. Shen argues the brain currently lags the body, bodies do not generalize, and if robots must own their own models, data must support scale-up. VA2.0 is framed as a robot-native stack (incl. MoE and causal attention), trained from random initialization; the robot GPT-1 moment remains open, with US–China approaches in dialogue.
background:
In 2026 China saw a wave of companies starting from robot brains — counter to the stereotype that overseas labs do brains and China does hardware. Last episode featured π researcher Ke Liyiming; this episode hosts Shen Yujun of Ant Lingbo (Ant-incubated), after a second-generation embodied/robot base model release, on building from random init and where the GPT-1 moment sits.

Shen's path: Tsinghua years overlapping SenseTime's founding, then CUHK under Tang Xiao'ou — from detection/segmentation leaderboards to GANs, editing, representation learning, and pretraining into robot-native models.
important_facts: Positioning: Ant Lingbo builds robot-native foundation models (VA series; interview centers VA2.0), stressing control/embodied bases trained from random initialization rather than only upper-layer fine-tunes. Versus π's open brain narrative, Lingbo is a domestic brain-first industrial sample backed by Ant incubation.

Core call: industry-wide the brain may currently lag the body; body designs do not generalize — the generalizable layer is the model. If the view that robots must own their own models holds, data must support that model — data scale-up (not rare handcrafted demos) is the bottleneck.

Stack and timing: VA2.0 discussion covers native MoE, causal attention, and related design bets. Against NLP's GPT-1→3.5 cadence, whether robotics has an analogous GPT-1 / 'ChatGPT moment' stays open — the show pairs 'native architecture' with a next bet on 'data-native'.

mental_model.name: Brain-First × Non-Generalizable Bodies × Data Must Carry the Model
mental_model.components: Admit hardware can 'move' while brain capability lags. Pursue cross-embodiment generalization via a self-owned base model rather than skin-deep hardware stacks. The data flywheel must match model ambition; native architecture (MoE/causal attention) is method — scale is the decider.
mental_model.application: Separate embodied bets into 'humanoid skin' vs 'native brain' companies; compare π and Lingbo on public model versions and task generalization, not fundraising alone. For China brain-first labs, ask whether data loops can support self-owned pretraining — not just papers or demo clips.

key_insights.view: The brain lags the body — counterintuitive, agenda-setting.
key_insights.question: What are China brain-first labs betting?
key_insights.answer: Making hardware move is relatively easy; generalizable intelligence remains scarce. Starting from the brain then filling the body flips the 'China only does bodies' story and explains why Lingbo treats the base model as the product.

key_insights.view: Own the model → own data that can carry it.
key_insights.question: Is the bottleneck rare demos or data?
key_insights.answer: Shen is explicit: if the view holds, data must support a self-owned model; scaling data well matters more than hoarding rare hardware.

key_insights.view: The robot GPT-1 moment is still unpriced.
key_insights.question: What does VA2.0 mean?
key_insights.answer: Native MoE + causal attention are engineering choices on the path to a robot GPT; whether the bar analogous to GPT-1 is cleared stays open — the next jump may be data-native.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Ant-incubated domestic robot-native base-model lab; VA2.0 release window + brain-first narrative vs π — Long as a scarce China 'brain' observation name
Robot-native pretraining and fleet inference still consume accelerators — Lingbo/π-class bases expand GPU demand even while OEMs stay private

golden_quotes: The brain may currently lag the body.
Its data must be able to support the model.
Where is the robot GPT-1 moment?
